GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2020-10-11T08:56:05Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: tokenbf_v2 index does not drop rows in aggregation query
Description: The tokenbf_v2 index does not drop rows when used in an aggregation query. That is, according to the query trace, it is used and rows are said to be dropped, but eventually all rows are scanned anyway as if the index didn't exist.

In my case I have a (large) table like:

```
CREATE TABLE MY_TABLE
(
    `Year` LowCardinality(String),
    `Route` String,
    `Count` Float64
)
ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree
PARTITION BY Year,
ORDER BY (Month, Route, Count),
INDEX route_index (Route) TYPE tokenbf_v1(256, 2, 0) GRANULARITY 1,
SETTINGS index_granularity = 128;
```

Route is a comma separated string of id's, like '242341,345223,12341'. There can be hundreds of id's in a Route.

When I query: 

`select Count(*) from MYTABLE where Year = '2020' and hasToken(Route, '12341')`

the query trace shows this:

Key condition: (column 2 in ['2020, '2020']), unknown, and
MinMax index condition: (column 0 in ['2020', '2020']), unknown, and
Index `route_index` has dropped 254959 granules.
Selected 1 parts by date, 1 parts by key, 17961 marks to read from 7839 ranges
Reading approx. 2299008 rows with 2 streams

which looks good, but then it proceeds to read all rows anyway:

Aggregated. 233990 to 1 rows (from 0.225 MiB) in 5.498 sec. (42560.946 rows/sec., 0.041 MiB/sec.)
Aggregated. 104612 to 1 rows (from 0.102 MiB) in 5.774 sec. (18119.055 rows/sec., 0.018 MiB/sec.)
Aggregated. 130101 to 1 rows (from 0.127 MiB) in 5.775 sec. (22529.594 rows/sec., 0.022 MiB/sec.)
Aggregator: Merging aggregated data
executeQuery: Read **34925324** rows, 16.27 GiB in 5.966 sec., 5853956 rows/sec., 2.73 GiB/sec.

Actually if I run the query like this, which does not invoke the route_index:

`select Count(*) from MYTABLE where Year = '2020' and Route LIKE '%12341%'`

in this case the query will be faster! The reason is it also scans all rows but does not have the extra first step of the tokenbf index.

Expected behaviour:

Since the tokenbf_v2 filter was able to skip 34925324 - 2299008 rows, which is 93% of the total number of rows, I expected the hasToken query to be faster than the LIKE query which didn't use any index.
I don't understand why the hasToken query, after initially dropping all those rows, proceeds to scan all rows anyway.
